qualification: Database row hashes and actual protected-object probes do not establish erasure of provider logs, backups, untracked objects, unlinked historic identifiers or processor copies. Those classes remain blocked pending their own reviewed inventory and adapter. Shared fence inventory count/rows describe subject attribution only: unmapped with zero descriptors does not mean zero global rows or settled work. The five shared operational classes are always blocked, have no subject selector or erasure adapter, and do not grant runtime table access. Member Realtime topic copies are attributable from retained member sessions after managed session loss; neither provider TTL nor a zero scoped count verifies erasure. Both new classes require blocked policy.
